name: circuit_16mm2_in_4mm2_terminal
text:
petra 0

# violates: circuit.terminal.conductor_area
# The lighting radial with its 2.5 mm2 cable replaced by 16 mm2, still landed in a lever
# terminal that clamps 0.2 to 4 mm2: the conductor does not fit the terminal.

design "workshop-lighting-radial" {
  owner "e.designer@example.org"
  environment indoor_dry
}

ambient in [10 degC, 40 degC] signed "site.manager@example.org" source "site survey 2026-09"

circuit lighting {
  supply mains voltage 230 V fault_current in [0 kA, 6 kA] signed "dno.liaison@example.org" source "DNO letter 2026-08-14"
  breaker cb1 part mcb.B10
  wire w1 cable cable.cu_pvc_16 length 18 m install install.clipped_direct
  terminal t1 part terminal.lever_4mm2_75C
  consumer lamps

  connect mains.out -> cb1.in
  connect cb1.out -> w1.a
  connect w1.b -> t1.wire
  connect t1.out -> lamps.in
}

load lamp_draw {
  on lighting.lamps current in [0 A, 10 A]
  signed "e.designer@example.org" source "luminaire schedule rev 3"
}

claim hot:  lighting.w1.temperature <= 70 degC under lamp_draw
claim drop: lighting.w1.voltage_drop <= 3 % under lamp_draw
violations: circuit.terminal.conductor_area
16 mm2 conductor in terminal.lever_4mm2_75C, which clamps 0.2 mm2 to 4 mm2 (registry, tagged judged)

name: joint_opens_under_load
text:
petra 0

# violates: bolt.tension.separation
# One M12 8.8 bolt tightened to at most 10 Nm clamps two steel plates against a 40 kN
# pull. The preload, at most 10 / (0.16 x 0.012 m) = 5.2 kN, cannot hold the plates
# together, so the joint opens and the bolt carries all 40 kN, 82 % of its 48.9 kN proof
# load, against the 70 % claimed. Petra's load share counts only Phi F = 8 kN of it.

design "joint-opens" {
  owner "m.engineer@example.org"
  environment indoor_dry
}

joint bracket {
  bolt bolt.M12_8_8 count 1
  plate steel.S355 thickness 10 mm
  plate steel.S355 thickness 10 mm
  torque in [5 Nm, 10 Nm] signed "fitter.lead@example.org" source "assembly spec AS-12 rev C"
  nut_factor in [0.16, 0.2] measured "test.lab@example.org" source "torque-tension report TT-2026-031"
  load_share in [0.1, 0.2] signed "m.engineer@example.org" source "joint diagram calc JD-7"
}

load pull {
  on bracket force in [0 kN, 40 kN]
  signed "client.structures@example.org" source "lifting study LS-2"
}

claim tension: bracket.tension_utilisation <= 0.7 under pull

waive bolt.plate_bearing on bracket by "m.engineer@example.org" reason "plates checked by hand, calc PB-3"
violations: bolt.tension.separation
preload down to 2.083 kN lets the joint open, so each bolt carries 40 kN, above the claimed 34.21 kN (the linear share gives 13.21 kN)

name: truss_600m_span
text:
petra 0

# violates: truss.self_weight
# The Warren truss example scaled to a 600 m span under 1 to 2 N per top node. Its 250 m
# diagonals of CHS 60.3x3.2 each weigh about 11 kN, which the truss model never loads.

design "warren-footbridge-panel" {
  owner "a.reviewer@example.org"
  environment indoor_dry
}

truss frame {
  material steel.S355
  section chs.60_3x3_2

  node A at (0 m, 0 m) support pinned
  node B at (300 m, 0 m)
  node C at (600 m, 0 m) support roller_x
  node D at (150 m, 200 m)
  node E at (450 m, 200 m)

  member bottom_ab: A -- B
  member bottom_bc: B -- C
  member top_de:    D -- E section chs.76_1x3_2
  member diag_ad:   A -- D
  member diag_db:   D -- B
  member diag_be:   B -- E
  member diag_ec:   E -- C
}

load crowd {
  on frame.D fy in [-2 N, -1 N]
  on frame.E fy in [-2 N, -1 N]
  signed "client.structures@example.org" source "brief rev B, section 3.2"
}

claim strength:   frame.collapse_factor >= 1.5 under crowd
claim stability:  frame.stability_factor >= 3 under crowd
claim stress:     frame.member(diag_ad).stress <= 235 MPa under crowd
violations: truss.self_weight
collapse factor 0 with the members' weight, below the claimed 1.5 (without it 3.109): the truss cannot carry its own weight
